The caterpillar weighs 10 pounds at the moment he eats his 10th fruit, which takes **9217 days**.

**Setup.** Let $p_k$ be the position of the $k$-th fruit he eats, with $p_0 = 0$ (the origin). The fruits are eaten in the order $1, -1, 2, -2, 3, -3, \dots$, so $|p_k| = \lceil k/2 \rceil$, and consecutive fruits lie on opposite sides of the origin. After eating $j$ fruits he weighs $j$ pounds and moves at speed $2^{-j}$. The leg from $p_j$ to $p_{j+1}$ therefore has distance $d_j = |p_j| + |p_{j+1}| = \lceil j/2 \rceil + \lceil (j+1)/2 \rceil$ and takes $d_j \cdot 2^j$ days.

**Legs for $j = 0, \dots, 9$:**

| $j$ | $d_j$ | time $d_j \cdot 2^j$ |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1 | 1 |
| 1 | 2 | 4 |
| 2 | 3 | 12 |
| 3 | 4 | 32 |
| 4 | 5 | 80 |
| 5 | 6 | 192 |
| 6 | 7 | 448 |
| 7 | 8 | 1024 |
| 8 | 9 | 2304 |
| 9 | 10 | 5120 |

**Total.** The sum of these times is
$$1+4+12+32+80+192+448+1024+2304+5120 = 9217.$$

ANSWER: 9217
